title: Asian Games 2026 in Japan: India's Complete Multi-Sport Schedule From Cricket to Athletics
excerpt: India will field athletes across more than 20 sporting disciplines at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games from September 19 to October 4, defending titles in cricket, kabaddi, and men's hockey.
body:
• The Asian Games 2026 run from September 19 to October 4 in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, with sporting action beginning September 10.
  • India will defend titles in men's and women's cricket, kabaddi, and men's hockey.
  • Key Indian stars include PV Sindhu (badminton), Mirabai Chanu (weightlifting), Manu Bhaker (shooting), and Aman Sehrawat (wrestling).
  • India's campaign begins with teqball on September 17, followed by women's cricket quarter-finals against Japan on September 18.

India's Title Defenses

India enters the 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan with defending titles in four team events: men's and women's cricket, men's and women's kabaddi, and men's hockey. The continental multi-sport event runs from September 19 to October 4, though competition begins as early as September 10 — nine days before the opening ceremony, according to Olympics.com.

India's campaign is scheduled to begin with teqball on September 17. The Indian women's cricket team will face Japan in the quarter-finals on September 18, with the men's quarter-final against the Group A runner-up on September 28.

Star Athletes to Watch

Two-time Olympic medallist PV Sindhu will headline India's badminton challenge, with competition at the Ichinomiya City Municipal Gymnasium scheduled from September 20. The badminton draw runs through September 29, with individual finals on the final day.

Olympic medallist Mirabai Chanu leads India's five-member weightlifting squad. Double Olympic medallist Manu Bhaker will be among the country's leading shooters. Paris 2024 bronze medallist Aman Sehrawat will represent India in wrestling.

"India's boxing contingent enters on the back of a record-breaking Commonwealth Games campaign, where Indian boxers won 10 medals — seven gold and three silver."

India's boxing contingent enters on the back of a record-breaking Commonwealth Games campaign, where Indian boxers won 10 medals — seven gold and three silver. Olympic medallist Lovlina Borgohain and Commonwealth Games champion Sakshi Chaudhary are among the confirmed boxers for Aichi-Nagoya.

Key Dates by Sport

Cricket: Women's quarter-final vs Japan on September 18, semi-finals September 20, final September 22. Men's quarter-final September 28, semi-final October 1, final October 3.

Hockey: Men's Pool A campaign opens September 20 against Indonesia, with matches against Sri Lanka (Sept 22), Korea (Sept 24), Japan (Sept 26), and Bangladesh (Sept 28). Women's Pool B starts September 20 against Uzbekistan. Medal matches on October 2-3.

Badminton: Team events from September 20-24 (finals September 24), individual events September 25-29.

Athletics: Track and field events run September 24-29 with more than 70 Indian athletes expected. Key events include the men's 100m final (September 25), men's marathon (September 26), javelin throw finals (September 28), and relay finals (September 29).

Boxing: Preliminary rounds from September 21, semi-finals September 29-30, all finals on October 2.

Kabaddi: Men's and women's group stages begin September 21, with knockout rounds and finals in late September.

Beyond the Marquee Sports

India will also compete in archery (September 26 to October 3), gymnastics (September 22-24), equestrian events (September 21-27), fencing (September 22-27), golf (September 30 to October 3), judo (September 30 to October 1), and track cycling (September 29 to October 2). Newer additions to the Asian Games program include esports, MMA, and kurash.

What to Watch For

India's medal prospects are strongest in badminton, boxing, weightlifting, shooting, wrestling, and hockey — sports where India has established competitive depth at the Olympic and Commonwealth Games level. Athletics, with its large contingent, offers multiple medal opportunities in javelin, relay events, and distance running.

The cricket competitions carry particular significance as India defends both titles in what remains a relatively new Asian Games sport. With the Games taking place in Japan — home to a growing cricket community — the host nation could pose an early challenge in the women's quarter-final on September 18.

For Indian fans worldwide, the Asian Games represent the last major multi-sport event before the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, making performances in Aichi-Nagoya an important indicator of India's broader sporting trajectory.
